codeReview.summary: The grapheme-preservation fix correctly addresses same-width viewport-to-scrollback rebasing, but it leaves stale scrollback grapheme indices behind when old history is trimmed to max_scrollback, so grapheme metadata can point at the wrong visible rows after subsequent full syncs.

issues.description: After rebasing viewport grapheme entries and adding scrollback graphemes, the code trims excess history with scrollback.pop_front() but never shifts or drops the corresponding grapheme_map indices. Because grapheme_map uses absolute buffer indices spanning scrollback plus viewport, trimming one or more oldest rows leaves every preserved scrollback entry offset too high, so a later render can attach a grapheme to the wrong row/cell. This regresses correctness whenever max_scrollback is reached during full-sync append handling.

The added regression only covers preserving a grapheme when a same-width full sync moves a viewport row into scrollback. It does not exercise the max_scrollback trimming path introduced by the fix, so the stale-index bug above remains untested and would not be caught by this feature's new coverage.

summary: Reviewed the review-ciri-app handoff, transcript skeleton, skill instructions, and commit 9ce43b4. The feature fixes one grapheme-loss case, but the new rebasing logic fails to renormalize grapheme_map when scrollback rows are trimmed, so the review fails on a blocking client-grid correctness bug.
